headline: Thursday the day — start the cool west corner, break's slid off
body:
Fog first: patchy dense fog both mornings, visibility a mile or less across the channel and outer waters — run radar and ease the throttle until it lifts. A small-craft advisory sits on the outer northwest waters from 3 PM through late tonight; that's well off our line, but it tells you wind builds late.

Wednesday inside the triangle is mild — channel seas 2–3 ft, west wind under 10, though the point stiffens to WNW 12 by mid-afternoon. Santa Rosa Flats and the outer banks run 4–6 ft and sloppier today. Thursday lays down nicer, the outer waters especially (W 5–10), triangle holding 2–3 ft.

So Thursday's the day. But the break has slid off — all three corners read warm: west 71.7, south 73.5, east 73.9, none near the 64–68 band. Start the west edge, south of Santa Cruz, on that coolest 71° water and grind on bait. Santa Rosa's no cooler and rougher; Osborn's the warmest. Stay in the triangle.
